newsitem.title: USA: Community group seeks to block NationsBank merger.
newsitem.headline: Community group seeks to block NationsBank merger.

text.p: Moments after bank regulators approved NationsBank Corp's proposed merger with Boatmen's Bancshares Inc on Monday, a community activist group said it would try to block the deal in court.
The group, Inner City Press/Community on the Move, said the Federal Reserve Board of Governors ignored evidence of discrimination in lending practices at NationsBank.
"We said to the Fed, 'We've shown enough evidence, you should go in and look,' but they did not," the group's executive director Matthew Lee said.
Lee declined to comment on where the lawsuit would be filed, saying only that it would be a federal appeals court.
The group will seek a temporary stay blocking the merger while the court reviews the case, Lee said.
The group has challenged previous bank mergers on the grounds that the resulting combinations would leave low-income neighborhoods underserved.
In a 45-page decision approving the merger, the Fed said 15 groups had criticized the lending performance of the banks in low income neighborhoods.
NationsBank has previously denied the charges. Bank officials called the group's charges "wild innuendo" and said the bank had a "strong record" on lending in low income and minority communities.
Lee said NationsBank had failed to notify the Fed of a pending class action lawsuit filed in Georgia against a subsidiary, Nationscredit Financial Services Corp.

In a letter dated Monday, NationsBank told the Fed that it was not required to disclose the lawsuit. "NationsBank has never provided, or was requested to provide, a list of all pending class action lawsuits," the letter said.
Lee said the bank's letter ignored the Fed's explicit instructions in a November 5 letter.

A copy of the letter, provided by Lee, asked the bank to provide the Fed with "a comprehensive update on the status of any and all judicial, administrative, or disciplinary proceedings," including "the resolution of such actions (if finalized)."

The Fed said its examiners had reviewed both banks' lending records, which are governed by the Community Reinvestment Act, and cited steps NationsBank has taken to boost lending to minority borrowers.
